s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia in March 2020
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye
Mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema
2 peripapillary hemorrhages and mild vitreous inflammation
Retinal vessel narrowing in the inferior retina
Normal complete blood cell counts and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts

shortlist.label: uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema

shortlist.label: sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has granulomatous-like symptoms such as relative afferent pupillary defect and central scotoma

shortlist.label: multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has optic neuritis symptoms such as blurred vision and pain when mobilizing the globe

shortlist.label: tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has severe respiratory infection and subsequent ocular involvement

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: patient has positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and severe bilateral pneumonia

raw.rationale: The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had a recent close contact with a fatal case, with a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, suggesting a COVID-19 infection. The development of blurred vision and redness in one eye, along with other ocular symptoms, could be related to COVID-19-associated ocular manifestations.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: While uveitis could explain some of the ocular symptoms, it does not account for the patient's pneumonia or the positive SARS-CoV-2 test.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis is not supported by the normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels or the lack of other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: Multiple sclerosis is not consistent with the patient's acute presentation or the normal cranial MRI results.

rejected.label: tuberculosis
rejected.why: Tuberculosis is not supported by the lack of relevant medical history or the negative laboratory tests for other infections.
